item.title: JJ Hanrahan gone for scan on hamstring
item.description: JJ Hanrahan is gone for a scan following his late withdrawl ahead of Munster's win over the Dragons on Friday night. The Kerryman has a hamstring strain, the extent of which should be known by tomorrow morning. item.title: Kerry racing news
item.description: Shuttle Diplomacy staked his claim for one of the big novice races at Cheltenham in March with a convincing success in the Irish EBF Maiden Hurdle over 2m2f at Naas on Sunday. Prepared by Tralee handler Tom Cooper, the gelding impressed with how he put away the well-backed 2-1 favourite Arcadian Emperor, trained by Willie Mullins for JP McManus, by over four lengths at odds of 11-4. item.title: Killarney Water Rescue Search and Recovery Team finds missing 6-year-old boy
item.description: A missing six-year-old boy was found in Muckross Park following a dramatic search by Killarney Water Rescue, Search and Recovery Team. The child wandered off from his family on the grounds of Muckross House, and KWR became aware that he was missing at round 4:15 yesterday afternoon. Nine people and four search dogs were involved, before the public also joined in. Advertisement Kieran Caulfield of KWR said it was good fortune that they were in the right place at the right time. item.title: Mark Allen into Round 2 of German Masters
item.description: Antrim's Mark Allen is into Round 2 of the German Masters. He beat Oliver Lines by 5 frames to 3 this afternoon. Fellow Ulsterman Jordan Brown takes on Masters semi-finalist Wu Yize this evening for a place in Round 2. Advertisement

item.title: Ireland defeat Namibia
item.description: Namibia were bowled out for 107 for 8 in their 20 overs by Ireland at the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup qualifier. Ireland chased down their target with ease to win by seven wickets in 14.2 overs. It's a third win for Ireland who are second in their group.
